## Problem statement

The proxy's `low` priority route (used by the priority-window cheap slot, 01:00–10:00 local, plus any explicit `X-Priority: low`) currently chains as `[local-qwen3, munitoai-free]` for the plan/author/code models. When the 2 local slots are saturated (a common overnight condition — see the 2026-10-19 proxy-usage-analysis report: `fallback_after_queue` 1657, `large_context_bypass` 1530, `context_too_large` 3393), low-priority traffic falls straight through to `munitoai-free`, which is capped at **`rate_limit_rpm: 2`** and is the last entry in the chain — so once its tiny budget is spent the request has nowhere else to go but an upstream 429 (16 upstream 429 events in the last window, all from `api.munito.ai`).

Meanwhile the three `opencode-go` entries (`opencode-go-3`, `opencode-go-2`, `opencode-go`) sit idle despite being available during their off-peak UTC windows (`["00:00-01:00", "04:00-06:00", "10:00-00:00"]`, added by LP-0MSXPHTD9004DZ4P) — which are precisely the hours when the cheap priority window is active and local is most contended.

Goal: allow low-priority work to fall back to **all** opencode models while they are inside their permissible (`available_times`) windows, so local-slot overflow during cheap hours is absorbed by idle paid capacity instead of being rate-limited on the free tier.

## Operator decisions (recorded)

- **Do NOT widen `available_times`.** The existing off-peak windows stay exactly as they are; paid spend remains confined to them.
- **Allow all opencode models on the low chain**, gated by those windows — not just one entry.

## Context / constraints

- `priority_routes.low` for plan/author/code is `[local-qwen3, munitoai-free]` (`proxy/config.yaml`); `munitoai-free` carries `rate_limit_rpm: 2`.
- Each of plan/author/code defines three equivalent opencode entries: `opencode-go-3` (OPENCODE_3_API_KEY), `opencode-go-2` (OPENCODE_2_API_KEY), `opencode-go` (OPENCODE_API_KEY) — same gateway, same model `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, same windows.
- **Why all three is meaningful (not cosmetic):** per LP-0MSMBWB23009XYPW / LP-0MVCX0E2V001VB5N, rate-limit quarantine is keyed on the **API-key account** (`_usage_limit_account_key` = `api_key_env@endpoint`), *not* the shared gateway domain. A 429 on one entry therefore poisons only that account, so its sibling keys are still tried with their own independent quota — i.e. 3× rate-limit capacity.
- **Counter-caveat to document:** for *non-rate-limit* failures (5xx, stalls) same-gateway siblings ARE skipped as one failure domain (`_failure_domain_key` / `attempted_domains`), so the three entries do **not** multiply capacity during an opencode outage. That is correct behaviour and must be stated in the config comments so nobody expects 3× resilience.
- **UTC-vs-local alignment (measured):** `available_times` are **UTC**; the cheap window (01:00–10:00) is **local `Europe/Dublin` = UTC 00:00–09:00**. opencode-go is unavailable UTC 01:00–04:00 and 06:00–10:00, so the new tiers add capacity in **~3 of the 9 cheap hours** (UTC 00:00–01:00 and 04:00–06:00). Accepted — the gaps are deliberate paid-spend avoidance, and the operator chose not to widen them.
- The `compact` model's low chain (`opencode-go-compact → deepseek-flash-compact`) is out of scope.
- The fully-paid `munitoai` and `deepseek-flash` entries must NOT join the low chain — they have no window discipline enforcing off-peak-only spend (`munitoai` has no `available_times` at all).

## Scope

Config + routing documentation + tests only. No llama-server changes, no `available_times` changes. Evidence via the proxy-usage-analysis skill (`python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py --hours 24`).

## Acceptance criteria

1. `priority_routes.low` for plan, author and code chains **all three** opencode entries, ordered after `munitoai-free`: `[local-qwen3, munitoai-free, opencode-go-3, opencode-go-2, opencode-go]`.
2. Every `available_times` value in `proxy/config.yaml` is **unchanged** by this work (no widening) — verifiable by diffing the config for `available_times` lines.
3. Unit tests prove window gating: inside a window the opencode entries are eligible; outside, they are skipped and the chain falls through exactly as today.
4. Unit tests prove per-key 429 failover: a 429 on `opencode-go-3` does not exclude `opencode-go-2`/`opencode-go` from the same request (independent account quota), while a 5xx on `opencode-go-3` DOES exclude them as one failure domain.
5. Chain order preserved: `local-qwen3` first when local has capacity; `munitoai-free` before any paid entry; `medium`/`high` chains byte-identical to before.
6. `munitoai` and `deepseek-flash` never appear in a `low` chain.
7. Config comments (and `priority.py::priority_routing_profile` docstring if it states the paid-tier invariant) document: the off-peak exception, the 3-of-9-hour UTC/local overlap, the per-key-429 capacity rationale, and the same-domain 5xx caveat.
8. Full suite passes via `/skill:test`; a post-change proxy-usage-analysis report is recorded on this item showing whether `rate_limited`/HTTP 429 from `api.munito.ai` fell during the overlap hours, with an honest "too small a sample" statement if not.

### Related work items
- **LP-0MVF1FQJR000NH2I** – Add opencode-go to low-priority routes (off-peak) (blocked)
- **LP-0MVF1FM9500070U1** – Test: off-peak low-priority fallback gating (open)

### Repository file matches

- `proxy/README.md` — matched: 5xx, accepted, account, active, add (+181 more)

- `proxy/tests/` — new window-gating, chain-order, per-key-429 and same-domain-5xx tests (owned by LP-0MVF1FM9500070U1).

# Intake brief: re-evaluate `session_slot_pool_size` using historical GPU busy-time and contention metrics

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the local slot-pool size (`session_slot_pool_size`, fixed at
**2** since LP-0MV9UNGEB009XUZ5 / LP-0MVCGYAI80084PCZ) re-decided on measured
evidence, so the GPU is sized to the real concurrent demand rather than to a
2026-10-17 snapshot.

## Problem statement

The N=2 verdict was made when the binding constraints were believed to be
(a) queue-timeout rate under 3 concurrent sessions (N=1: 70.6–75%, N=2: 20–25%)
and (b) N=3's per-slot context clamp (83,285). Both premises are now questionable:

1. **Demand exceeds the pool far more often than assumed.** From
   `/var/log/llama-proxy` for 2026-10-19 07:23 → 2026-10-20 07:23 (348 sessions,
   17,580 requests), reconstructing per-session in-flight intervals:
   - peak concurrent sessions with an in-flight request: **7**
   - mean concurrency **2.15**; **37.2% of minutes had >2** concurrent sessions
   - by session class, peak concurrency: `herdr-*` panes **6**, `audit-*` subagents
     **3**, operator/pi/LAN sessions **4**
2. **The pool refuses work while the GPU is not decoding**: `local_dispatch_denied`
   **2,641** times (2,633 with `active=2`), `local_lease_active` skips 1,949,
   contention-queue waits 5,805, of which **4,947 fell back remote** and only 855
   dispatched after the wait.
3. **The reported busy figure understates GPU work.** The report's 29.3% busy
   counts only `Stream started → Stream finished`. Local prefill is logged
   separately as `dispatch_first_byte_ms` and totals **14.3 h** across 463 local
   requests (median 61.8 s, p90 269.8 s, max 817 s). Adding prefill to the 7 h 47 m
   of decode puts real slot occupancy at roughly **79,500 s ≈ 46% of the 48
   slot-hours** available, not 16%.
4. **The queue timeout is shorter than a typical local slot hold.** Median
   dispatch→first-byte is 61.8 s, so a 120 s contention-queue wait
   (`contention_queue_max_wait_seconds: 120`) very often expires before a slot
   frees — consistent with 4,947 queue abandonments vs 855 queue dispatches.

## Task

Produce an evidence-backed slot-count decision (N=2 baseline vs N=3, and N=4 if
memory allows) from the historical record, not a fresh guess.

### Data sources to mine

- `~/proxy-usage-reports/` — **157 archived daily reports** (`YYYY-MM-DD[_n]/report.md`)
  spanning slot-config eras (fast=1/cheap=3 → converged 2). Each carries busy time
  (total / fast / cheap), `Queued → dispatched local`, `Fallback after queue`,
  local-serve share, and decode/prompt-eval speed. Sample already extracted:
  2026-09-01 62.1% busy / 39 queued-dispatched; 2026-10-09 91.6% / 9,556;
  2026-10-14 30.3% / —; 2026-10-17 18.8%; 2026-10-19 68.9%; 2026-10-20 29.3% / 855.
- `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log*` (7-day retention) — per-request
  `dispatch_first_byte_ms`, `local_dispatch_denied`, `contention_queue_*`,
  `lease_*`, `routing_skip_local`.
- `docs/slot-count-verdict-lp-0mv9ungeb009xuz5.md` — the N=2 sweep method and its
  fidelity caveats (must be reused so the new run is comparable).
- llama-server logs for eval/decode timings (largely absent this window — see the
  separate prefill-aware-metrics item).

### Acceptance criteria

1. A historical table of at least 20 archived report days with columns: date, slot
   config in force, mode split, GPU busy %, decode-vs-prefill split where
   available, `local_dispatch_denied`, queue depth/waits, `fallback_after_queue`,
   local serve share. Committed under `docs/` with the extraction script.
2. A concurrency-vs-capacity statement derived from logs: minutes-at-N-concurrent
   distribution, peak, and the share of demand that would still be denied at N=2
   vs N=3 vs N=4.
3. A measured N=3 (and N=4 if feasible) sweep using the same harness as the prior
   verdict, recording: local TTFT (`dispatch_first_byte_ms`), decode tok/s,
   queue-timeout rate, denials, `finish_reason=length` count, llama-server
   startup/`--parallel` agreement, per-slot KV memory and system MemAvailable.
4. A recorded decision (keep N=2 / move to N=3 / N=4) that states the expected
   effect on: local serve share, queue abandonment rate, per-slot context clamp
   (126,976 at N=2 vs 83,285 at N=3 — and therefore the interacting warm-threshold
   item), and VRAM headroom. If the decision is "keep N=2", enumerate the
   mitigations it depends on.
5. No change is made to production slot counts in this item — the deliverable is
   the decision record plus a follow-up item (if the decision is to change N).

## Risks / notes

- N=3 shrinks per-slot context to 83,285, which interacts directly with the
  "warm threshold = 95% of per-slot" item: at N=3 that target becomes 83,012, i.e.
  roughly today's effective ceiling. The two items must be decided together.
- Slots must match llama-server `--parallel` (`start-llama.sh`/`LLAMA_PARALLEL`);
  a mismatch silently wastes or breaks slots (documented in `proxy/config.yaml`).
- Prior sweeps could not isolate local decode share because live sessions held the
  dispatch leases; the new run must hold the mode lock / drain evidence or record
  the same validity caveat.

# Intake brief: seed `cached_ratio` from the persisted local slot snapshot

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want a session that already has a warm prefix in a saved local
slot snapshot to be scored as **warm** at routing time, so it is not bypassed to
remote on the false assumption that its whole prompt must be pre-filled again.

## Problem statement

The cold-cache gate derives `new_tokens = estimated_tokens × (1 − cached_ratio)`,
where `cached_ratio` comes only from `_last_cached_ratio` — an in-memory dict keyed
`(model, session)` that is written **solely** from `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`
on a *previous local response* (`provider.py::_get_cached_ratio`, default `0.0`).

Consequences measured in the window 2026-10-19 07:23 → 2026-10-20 07:23:

- **82.8%** of routing decisions had `cached_ratio=0.00` (5,627 of 6,799), i.e. the
  proxy almost always assumes a full cold prefill.
- Any session crossing 38,000 tokens is therefore permanently bypassed
  (`large_context_bypass`, 1,284 events), even when a slot snapshot for it exists and
  would let llama-server reuse its KV prefix.
- The proxy **already persists and restores slot state**: `session_slot_save_path`
  / `LLAMA_SLOT_SAVE_PATH` (`lifecycle.py`), `_restore_slot_snapshot` and `slot_save`
  (`router.py`), plus `/slots` polling that reads `n_past` / `kv_cache_tokens`
  (`observability.py`, `router_helpers.py`). The information needed to score a
  session as warm is available and simply is not used by the router.
- The in-memory dict is also lost on every proxy restart, so restarts reset the
  whole fleet to "cold" (3 manual restarts in the window), even though the KV
  snapshots survive on disk.

## Proposed change

At session (re)attach — and whenever a local dispatch is about to be gated — seed the
routing ratio from persisted/observed slot state:

1. On `_restore_slot_snapshot` success (or on first request of a session with an
   existing snapshot), read the slot's cached token count (`n_past` /
   `kv_cache_tokens`) and record
   `cached_ratio = min(1.0, cached_tokens / estimated_tokens)` for
   `(model, session)`, with a documented safety margin (only count tokens that are a
   true prefix of the incoming prompt; never assume more than the observed value).
2. Label the source in logs (`cache_state=restored` vs `warm` vs `cold`) so the
   report can separate restored-prefix wins from genuine cache hits.
3. Persist the ratio alongside the slot snapshot so a proxy restart does not reset
   warmness to 0 (optional, if the snapshot itself is authoritative).

## Acceptance criteria

1. A session with a restored slot snapshot whose `n_past` covers ≥ the cold threshold
   fraction no longer emits `routing_skip_local ... reason=large_context_bypass`.
2. Correctness guard: a snapshot that does **not** prefix-match the incoming prompt
   (changed system prompt / truncated history) must not be credited — either detect
   it (prefix hash) or fall back to `cached_ratio=0`; a test covers the mismatch case.
3. Never over-credit: `cached_ratio` from restoration is capped by the measured
   `cached_tokens / estimated_tokens`; a unit test asserts the cap.
4. Logs distinguish `cache_state=restored`; `proxy-usage-analysis` can report restored
   vs cold counts (coordinate with LP-0MVGCQ421005IXGC).
5. Before/after over ≥24h: share of routing decisions with `cached_ratio=0`
   (baseline 82.8%), `large_context_bypass` count (baseline 1,284), local serve share
   (baseline 2.6%), and local `dispatch_first_byte_ms` percentiles (a restored hit
   must show materially lower prefill time, baseline median 61.8 s).
6. Works across a proxy restart: a session resuming after restart is scored warm when
   its snapshot is present and valid.

## Risks / notes

- Wrong credits cause a **full re-prefill anyway** (correctness is preserved, latency
  is not) — hence AC2's prefix check.
- llama.cpp can invalidate its own checkpoints (`forcing full prompt re-processing`
  is expected on this hybrid-architecture Qwen3 per `AGENTS.md`); a restored snapshot
  is not a guarantee of a zero-cost prefix. Measure, do not assume.
- `slot_save failed` (5 events in the window, ReadTimeout) shows save/restore is not
  always reliable; the change must degrade to today's behaviour on failure.

# Intake brief: idle-aware local admission (serve large/cold prompts when the GPU is idle)

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want an oversized (or cache-cold) prompt to be admitted to the local
model **when the GPU has demonstrably been idle**, so idle capacity is spent instead
of a paid remote call.

## Problem statement

Routing is purely size/economics-driven and ignores whether the backend is doing
anything. So a prompt is bypassed even while both slots sit unused for minutes, and
requests are refused for slot occupancy even when the GPU never produced a token.

Measured window 2026-10-19 07:23 → 2026-10-20 07:23:

- Local compute was 7h47m of 48 slot-hours (decode only) and report busy 29.3%; with
  prefill included (`dispatch_first_byte_ms` sum **14.3 h**) real occupancy is ≈46%,
  i.e. the GPU is still idle more than half the window.
- `local_dispatch_denied` **2,641** (2,633 with both slots held), yet the 04:00–05:00
  hour logged **187** denials while local busy was **2.5%**.
- `proxy/config.yaml` already records the same finding from an earlier analysis:
  "Log analysis (5.3h, 198 local_dispatch_denied events) showed **100% of denies
  caused by idle lease holders, never GPU saturation** (active>=3: 0)", with
  inter-turn reclaim gaps of median 0.2 s / p95 1.6 s.
- Both `large_context_bypass` (1,284) and a share of `context_too_large` (2,463) skips
  therefore go remote while the model is idle — the exact inversion of the intended
  economics.

## Proposed change

Add an **idle-aware override** to the local routing gate:

1. Track `last_local_activity_ts` (last dispatch, last chunk/first byte, or last
   stream finish; whichever is latest) and expose it on `/llama/local/status`.
2. In `_should_skip_local`, if the backend has been idle longer than
   `local_idle_admit_seconds` (suggested default 60 s) **and** no request is queued,
   return `(False, None)` for the economic band (`large_context_bypass`) and — as a
   separately configurable and default-off step — for a bounded slice above the warm
   threshold.
3. Emit a distinct, greppable log line (`routing_idle_admit reason=… idle_seconds=…`)
   and count it in the report so the effect is auditable.
4. Fail safe: never override when a queue is non-empty, when the last local attempt
   failed, or when the model is loading/switching.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Config knobs `server.local_idle_admit_enabled` (default false) and
   `server.local_idle_admit_seconds` (default 60) are added, documented, and validated
   (non-negative; disabled when the local model is not healthy).
2. Unit tests: idle > threshold + empty queue ⇒ local admitted; idle < threshold ⇒
   today's bypass; queue non-empty ⇒ today's bypass; model loading ⇒ today's bypass.
3. The override is visible in logs and in `proxy-usage-analysis` (a counter for
   idle-admitted requests), and cannot fire while a hold/lease or prefill is in flight.
4. Before/after over ≥24h: local serve share (baseline 2.6%), idle share of the window
   (baseline ~54% of slot-hours), remote fallback count (baseline 17,076), and
   `dispatch_first_byte_ms` percentiles for idle-admitted requests (they will be slow —
   that is expected; record it).
5. No increase in `local_dispatch_denied` and no increase in mid-stream timeouts
   (`ReadTimeout`, `empty_response`) attributable to the override.

## Risks / notes

- An idle-admitted 120K prompt can occupy a slot for many minutes (observed local
  prefill p90 269.8 s, max 817 s), which can block an interactive request that arrives
  one second later. Mitigations to evaluate in the same change: only admit while the
  contention queue is empty *and* the lease pool has a free slot; cap the admitted
  prompt size; prefer `low` priority.
- Overlaps with LP-0MVGCOZMZ003I6PF (warm threshold 95% of per-slot) and the
  `medium` economic-bypass item: this is the "GPU is idle now" complement to those
  static thresholds. Sequence them so each effect is measurable separately.
- Requires a truthful idle signal; see LP-0MVGCQ421005IXGC (prefill-aware metrics) —
  today's "busy" conflates decode-only with real occupancy.

# Intake brief: serialise local prefills so one prefill at a time gets the full GPU

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want at most one local **prefill** to run at a time (while other
slots may keep decoding), so each request's prefill gets full GPU throughput instead
of sharing it — cutting time-to-first-byte roughly in half with no loss of aggregate
throughput.

## Evidence (window 2026-10-19 07:23 → 2026-10-20 07:23, 460 paired local dispatches)

Prefill intervals (`dispatch_first_byte_ms`, reconstructed as `[t − dur, t]`) bucketed
by how many other local prefills overlapped them:

| Overlapping prefills | n | first-byte p50 | throughput (new tok/s, p50) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 | 190 | **23.4 s** | **253.8** |
| 1 | 220 | 85.0 s | 156.6 |
| 2 | 48 | 119.7 s | 128.8 |
| 3 | 2 | 222.2 s | 30.9 |

- **47.8% of local prefills (220/460) shared the GPU with at least one other**
  prefill; 50 shared it with two or more.
- Aggregate throughput is **flat** (≈254 → ≈258 tok/s) while per-request throughput
  halves — i.e. concurrency adds latency, not capacity.
- Observed total prefill wall time 50,645 s vs 21,600 s if every request had run at
  the solitary 254 tok/s → **2.3× inflation** from contention plus coded-context read
  cost.

## Proposed change

Add an admission semaphore for the **prefill phase only**:

1. Track per-slot phase from the existing `/slots` poll (`is_processing`,
   `n_past`/`n_prompt_tokens_processed`, coalesced per `SLOTS_POLL_TTL_SECONDS`).
2. Allow at most `server.local_max_concurrent_prefills` (default **1**) requests in
   prefill across the pool; a request whose slot would start a second concurrent
   prefill waits (bounded) or falls back per policy.
3. A slot already decoding does not block another slot's prefill — only
   prefill-vs-prefill is serialised, so decode keeps running in parallel.
4. Emit `prefill_gate_wait_ms` per request and expose the queue depth on
   `/llama/local/status`.

## Acceptance criteria

1. New config knob `server.local_max_concurrent_prefills` (default 1, 0 disables),
   documented, with validation.
2. Unit tests for the gate: second concurrent prefill waits; a decoding slot does not
   block; a request that cannot be admitted within its budget falls back exactly as
   today; disable → current behaviour.
3. Measured effect over ≥24h via `proxy-usage-analysis`: local `dispatch_first_byte_ms`
   p50/p90 (baseline p50 **61.8 s**, p90 **269.8 s**), share of prefills with ≥1
   overlap (baseline 47.8%), local serve share (baseline 2.6%), decode throughput
   (must not regress), and aggregate prefill tokens/s (must not regress).
4. No increase in `downloaded`/queue abandonment (`contention_queue_fallback_after_queue`,
   baseline 4,947) — the gate must not simply move the wait elsewhere.
5. Interaction recorded with the lease system: the gate must never hold a slot while
   the pool is otherwise idle (test covers "single request alone → no added delay").

## Risks / notes

- With 2 slots, serialising prefills means one slot may idle during a long prefill
  while the other decodes; that is the intended trade (throughput is flat anyway).
- Must not starve large prefills: a 7-minute prefill blocks the gate for 7 minutes;
  combine with a prefill-ETA-aware queue (see the admission-guard item) so queued
  requests with no chance of admission fall back immediately.
- Do not confuse this gate with the existing dispatch lease (session-scoped) or the
  contention queue (slot-scoped) — this one is phase-scoped.
data.title: Serialise local prefills so one prefill at a time gets the full GPU

# Intake brief: prefill-ETA-aware admission guard (stop starting local work that cannot finish in budget)

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the proxy to refuse local admission — immediately, with a
retryable hint — when the projected prefill wait cannot fit the caller's wait budget,
so requests stop burning up to 120 s in the contention queue only to fall back to
remote anyway, and slots stop starting prefills that will be abandoned.

## Evidence (window 2026-10-19 07:23 → 2026-10-20 07:23)

- Contention queue: **5,805** waits → **855** dispatched after the wait,
  **4,947** (`85%`) abandoned after up to 120 s and then went remote.
- Local prefill reality vs the 120 s queue cap: p50 **61.8 s**, p90 **269.8 s**,
  max **817 s**; projected cost for a 110k-token cold prompt is ~430 s
  (254 new tok/s solitary, 1.1 ms per coded context token).
- So for most queued requests the queue cannot succeed inside its own budget: the
  wait is a guaranteed loss of up to 120 s of client latency.
- Remote comparison: median remote TTFT **27 ms**, p90 **1.4 s** — waiting 120 s to
  maybe avoid a 27 ms call is a bad bet unless the prompt is genuinely cache-warm.

## Proposed change

Before entering the contention queue (and before a dispatch that would start a
second concurrent prefill), compute a **prefill ETA** and compare it with a wait
budget:

```
eta_prefill = est_tokens * coded_ms_per_token + new_tokens * prefill_ms_per_token
              (calibrated from recent local dispatches; window values 1.1 ms and 3.9 ms)
admit  if eta_prefill + decode_remaining <= wait_budget
else   return 429/503 + Retry-After immediately with X-Local-Admission guidance
```

- `wait_budget` = the caller's queue budget (existing
  `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds`) clamped by `X-Priority` semantics: `high`
  never queues (today), `medium`/`low` use the budget.
- Cache-warm requests (high `cached_ratio`) stay admissible because their
  `new_tokens` term is small — locality where it actually pays.
- Publish the estimate (`prefill_eta_seconds`, `queue_eta_seconds`) on
  `/llama/local/status` so dispatchers can pace before launching a session.

## Acceptance criteria

1. ETA calibration is data-driven: per-model/per-context-bucket coefficients derived
   from recent `dispatch_first_byte_ms` samples (rolling window), with sane defaults
   and a fallback to today's behaviour when insufficient samples exist.
2. Admission decision and reason are logged (`local_admission_guard decision=admit|reject
   eta_prefill_s=… budget_s=…`) and counted in the usage report.
3. Unit tests: ETA above budget ⇒ immediate reject with retryable status and
   `Retry-After`; ETA within budget ⇒ unchanged queue behaviour; `high` priority ⇒
   never queues (regression guard); missing calibration ⇒ unchanged behaviour.
4. Measured effect over ≥24h: `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue` (baseline 4,947)
   drops substantially; p50/p90 client-visible latency for guard-rejected requests
   approaches the remote TTFT baseline instead of ~120 s; local serve share does not
   fall below 2.6%; no increase in mid-stream errors.
5. The guard never rejects a request whose `cached_ratio` implies a cheap prefill
   (test with a 90%-cached 100k prompt: admitted).

## Risks / notes

- The ETA is a model, not a measurement: it must be conservative (prefer fallback) and
  must self-correct from observed `dispatch_first_byte_ms` rather than a fixed constant.
- Requires truthful idle/prefill signals; coordinate with the per-slot status item and
  the prefill-serialisation item (both change the wait landscape).
- Rejecting fast is a UX improvement over a silent 120 s stall, but it makes remote
  spend *visible* — record the spend delta so the trade is explicit.
data.title: Prefill-ETA admission guard: stop starting local work that cannot finish in budget

# Intake brief: re-widen local size gates only once cache warmth is proven (capacity-gated)

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I still want large prompts (38K–124K tokens) served locally **when the
GPU can actually absorb them** — but only after cache-warmth work has cut the cost per
request, and with admission sized to measured capacity rather than to a fixed token
threshold.

## Why this replaces the two deleted widening items

The previously filed items — "warm threshold to 95% of per-slot context"
(LP-0MVGCOZMZ003I6PF, deleted) and "economic bypass for medium priority"
(LP-0MVGD9YLM0055SFF, deleted) — were deleted because, as scoped, they widen admission
faster than the GPU can absorb, which makes cache churn and first-token latency worse:

| Band | Requests / 24h | Median prompt | Cold cost at 254 new tok/s | Slot-hours needed | Prefill headroom available |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 100,000–124,518 (`context_too_large`) | 890 | ~110k | ~430 s each | **~107 h** | ~26 h |
| 38,000–100,000 (`large_context_bypass`) | 1,284 | ~71k | ~280 s each | **~100 h** | ~26 h |

Headroom = 48 slot-hours/day − 28,020 s decode − 50,645 s measured prefill ≈ 26 h
(≈23.8 M new tokens at 254 tok/s). Both bands are ~4× over capacity **cold**, and ≈10
slot-hours each at a 90% cache-hit rate — i.e. they fit *only* with warm caches.

## Preconditions (blocking)

1. **Cache warmth**: `cached_ratio` seeded from persisted slot snapshots
   (LP-0MVGD9YXH008O304) — measured by the share of local dispatches that are
   `cache_state=cold` (baseline **45.7%**, 210/460).
2. **Admission control**: prefill-ETA-aware admission guard (the "stop starting local
   work that cannot finish in budget" item) so a widened gate cannot turn into
   queue-then-fallback stalls.
3. **Prefill protection**: prefill serialisation so widened admission does not halve
   per-request prefill throughput via contention (baseline: 47.8% of prefills shared the
   GPU, p50 85 s with one overlap vs 23.4 s alone).

## Proposed change (only after the preconditions land)

Replace the two fixed token thresholds' *effective* behaviour with a **capacity-aware
admission** rule layered on the existing thresholds:

- Keep `context_too_large` as the hard physical cap (`ctx // slots − 4096` = 126,976).
- For the economic band, admit locally while the projected slot-hours of admitted
  traffic stay within a configured share of idle capacity (e.g.
  `local_capacity_admission_budget_ratio: 0.8` of measured idle slot-time), and fall
  back to remote when the projection exceeds it.
- Raise the warm threshold toward 95% of per-slot (124,518 at N=2) **only** as the
  measured cache-hit rate supports it; report the achieved setting.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Preconditions evidenced in comments before implementation starts: cold-dispatch
   share materially below 45.7%, admission guard live, prefill serialisation live.
2. The admission rule is capacity-based, not threshold-only: a projection exceeding the
   configured idle-slot budget routes remote early, and the projection is recomputed from
   rolling observed data (no fixed constant).
3. Measured over ≥24h after enabling: local serve share rises from 2.6%; `cache_state=cold`
   share does **not** rise above the 45.7% baseline; `dispatch_first_byte_ms` p50/p90 do
   **not** regress beyond a stated budget (baseline 61.8 s / 269.8 s); queue abandonment
   does **not** exceed the 4,947 baseline; `finish_reason=length` stays at zero.
4. A rollback switch (`local_capacity_admission_enabled`) with a documented revert path.
5. The achieved warm threshold and the reason for it (measured hit-rate) are recorded in
   the config comment and in the item.

## Risks / notes

- This is deliberately a *follow-on* item: implementing it first reproduces the harm the
  deleted items would have caused.
- Compaction is the complementary lever (reduces `est_tokens` rather than cost/token);
  the compaction dry-run currently reports 110/347 sessions that would have triggered —
  that is the potential supply-side reduction to weigh against local admission.
data.title: Re-widen local size gates only once cache warmth is proven (capacity-gated)

# Increase `munitoai-free` `rate_limit_rpm` to 3

## Problem statement

The `munitoai-free` (MunitoAI free-tier) remote fallback provider entry is
currently capped at **2 requests per rolling 60-second window**
(`rate_limit_rpm: 2`, set by LP-0MVF19DKR008VCHO after an earlier reduction
from 15). This cap is deliberately conservative, but at only 2/min the free
tier's actual upstream allowance (~150 k input tokens per rolling 60 s, probed
2026-10-19) is routinely unused while requests spill to the paid tiers. The
operator wants the budget raised to **3/min** — a modest bump that stays far
below the measured upstream 429 onset (~20 dispatches/rolling 60 s).

## Users

- **Proxy operator** (primary): wants the free tier used closer to its real
  allowance without burning the quiet allowance on bursts or pushing the
  upstream into 429s.

  User story: *"As the proxy operator, I want `munitoai-free` to accept up to 3
  requests per minute so that normal agent work spills to the paid tiers less
  often, while bursts still spill rather than hammering the free tier."*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. All three `munitoai-free` entries in `proxy/config.yaml` (the `plan`,
   `author` and `code` chains) declare `rate_limit_rpm: 3`.
2. Inline config comments that quote the 2/min budget (the
   "Deliberately conservative at 2/min" and "full 2-per-window cap" notes,
   ref. LP-0MVF19DKR008VCHO) are updated to describe 3/min with the same
   conservative rationale; the reserve arithmetic comment stays accurate
   (`floor(3 × 0.3) = 0` reserve slots, so new and in-progress sessions both
   see the full 3-per-window cap).
3. `proxy/docs/routing.md` and `proxy/README.md` are updated wherever they
   quote `2` (budget of 2/min, `rate_limit_rpm: 2`, `2 of 2`, value-history
   notes) so shipped value and reserve/cap arithmetic state 3 correctly.
4. The MunitoAI fallback-chain test fixture (`MUNITOAI_FREE_ENTRY` in
   `proxy/tests/test_munitoai_fallback_chain.py`, which pins the exact resolved
   entry via `providers[1] == MUNITOAI_FREE_ENTRY`) is updated to
   `rate_limit_rpm: 3`, and the changed-scope test gate passes.
5. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.
6. Commit recorded on this work item and pushed to `dev` (takes effect at the
   next proxy restart).

## Constraints

- This item tunes **one number** — do not change the gate, the reserve ratio,
  the wait caps or any other provider entry.
- The paid `munitoai` tier declares no `rate_limit_rpm` and is out of scope.
- Never drive the third-party free tier into sustained 429s.

## Existing state

- `proxy/config.yaml`: `rate_limit_rpm: 2` on all three `munitoai-free`
  entries (lines ~390, ~582, ~748 — one per chain, sharing one bucket keyed on
  the provider entry name).
- `proxy/tests/test_munitoai_fallback_chain.py:45`: `MUNITOAI_FREE_ENTRY` pins
  `"rate_limit_rpm": 2` and is asserted against the resolved config for all
  three chains and both merged profiles — must move to 3 in lockstep.
- Docs quoting the value: `proxy/docs/routing.md` (lines ~101, ~113, ~129,
  ~131, ~139, ~220) and `proxy/README.md` (~line 520, "2 of 2").

## Desired change

Change `rate_limit_rpm: 2` → `rate_limit_rpm: 3` on the three `munitoai-free`
entries in `proxy/config.yaml`, sync the inline comments, the pinned test
fixture, and the docs that quote the shipped value.

## Key Files

- `proxy/config.yaml` — `rate_limit_rpm: 2` → `3` on the three `munitoai-free`

## User story

As an operator running many concurrent agent sessions against a 2-slot local
Qwen3 backend, I need a session that already holds (or has just released) a
local dispatch lease to be re-admitted ahead of a newcomer, so that a
returning session does not burn the full contention-queue budget and detour
to a paid remote provider — and then come back and re-prefill — repeatedly
within a single session.

## Observed behaviour (routing thrash)

Session `audit-WL-0MVFRRKKN00544PQ-phase2_child_5-6e22ef57` (2026-10-21,
12:23:35–12:36:55) alternated local ↔ remote **7 times in 12 minutes**:

| # | time | provider | trigger |
|---|------|----------|---------|
| 1 | 12:24:29 | local Qwen3 | `contention_queue_dispatch queued_duration=48.37s` |
| 2 | 12:25:27 | local Qwen3 | `contention_queue_dispatch queued_duration=48.96s` |
| 3 | 12:27:30 | MunitoAI Free | `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue queued_duration=120.00s` |
| 4 | 12:28:06 | local Qwen3 | reclaim, `cached_ratio=0.513`, 35.8 s prefill |
| 5 | 12:30:30 | OpenCode Go 3 | `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue queued_duration=120.00s` |
| 6 | 12:34:43 | OpenCode Go 3 | `local_dispatch_denied ... owner=audit-WL-0MVFRRMX3003UPP3-phase2_child_6 active=1` |
| 7 | 12:34:48 | local Qwen3 | reclaim, `cached_ratio=0.396`, 2.2 s prefill |

Every hop was **not** a context-size or ETA-guard decision: the
`local_admission_guard` returned `decision=admit reason=within_budget` at
3.9 s / 9.8 s / 11.0 s / 66.7 s / 72.9 s on every attempt, and prompts were
only 2,067–20,468 tokens (far below `local_large_context_cold_cache_threshold`
38000). The binding constraint was **dispatch contention**: the slot was held
by another session (`local_lease_active`, `local_dispatch_denied owner=<other
session>`), so the request waited the full `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds`
(120 s) and then fell through to the remote chain.

Cost per hop: a wasted 120 s queue wait, a paid remote round-trip, plus a
re-prefill on return (35.8 s at 12:28:06, 2.2 s at 12:34:48). It also erodes
the session's own cached-prefix bookkeeping (`cached_ratio` fell 0.513 → 0.396
across one remote detour).

## Root cause hypothesis

The contention queue orders by arrival, not by cache locality or prior lease
ownership. A session that has just released its local lease (`lease_released
reason=idle_timeout`) and immediately returns re-queues behind newcomers, even
though its KV prefix is still resident and its own prefill would be far
cheaper than a newcomer's cold prefill. With 2 slots and 3+ active sessions
this starves returning sessions deterministically.

## Proposed fix

1. **Lease-owner retention priority** — a session with an active lease, or one
   released within a configurable grace window (e.g.
   `contention_queue_lease_grace_seconds`), is dispatched ahead of a session
   with no local cache history in the contention queue.
2. **Skip the futile wait** — when a returning session is queued behind a
   newcomer whose prefill will not finish inside the returning session's
   budget, refuse immediately (as the prefill-ETA guard already does for
   over-budget ETAs) instead of waiting the full 120 s.
3. **Observability** — emit a log line when the retention priority reorders
   the queue, so the behaviour is auditable and countable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1: A session with an active local lease, or a lease released within
      `contention_queue_lease_grace_seconds` (new config knob, default
      documented), is dispatched ahead of a newcomer in the contention queue;
      the reorder emits a log line naming both sessions and the reason.
- [ ] AC2: Unit test: session A takes and releases a local lease, session B
      queues with no cache history, A returns — A is dispatched first. Asserted
      on dispatch order, and the log line from AC1 is present.
- [ ] AC3: Unit test: a returning session whose prefix has genuinely been
      evicted (no cached-ratio record, no slot sidecar) is not held ahead of a
      newcomer and still falls through without burning the full
      `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds`.
- [ ] AC4: Regression test: when the prefill-ETA guard refuses admission
      (`eta_exceeds_budget`), the remote fallback still happens immediately —
      no new queue wait is introduced by the priority change.
- [ ] AC5: The routing-thrash pattern is measurable: the proxy-usage report (or
      an equivalent aggregate) counts local↔remote provider transitions per
      session, so the 7-hop case above is detectable without manual log
      archaeology.
- [ ] AC6: Replaying/observing the recorded case (or a synthetic equivalent)
      shows fewer than 3 provider transitions where 7 occurred before.
- [ ] AC7: `config.yaml` documents the new knob(s) with the default and a
      rollback path; changed-scope tests and the full suite pass.

## Related finding (separate item)

The second turn of this session also routed with `cached_ratio=0.00` despite
turn 1 having completed locally — the ratio is recorded from the *previous*
response's measured `cached_tokens`, so a genuinely cold first turn writes
0.0 and turn 2 inherits it. See the accompanying `discovered-from` item.

## Defect

`contention_queue_lease_grace_seconds` (added by LP-0MVI2VRT2000V1AP) is
clamped by `_get_contention_queue_config` to `[0, contention_queue_max_wait_seconds]`
(120). The shipped config value is **300**, so every call emits:

```
WARNING - contention_queue_lease_grace_seconds=300 clamped to 120.0
          (bounds [0, contention_queue_max_wait_seconds=120.0])
```

`_get_contention_queue_config` runs **per request** (and per status poll), so
the warning fires continuously — measured on the restart at 2026-10-21
14:47: **36 warnings within seconds**. It pollutes the log, will trip
rate-based alerting on the WARNING stream, and contradicts both the
`config.yaml` comment and `docs/dev/contention-queue-lease-retention.md`,
which state 300 s is the default and is deliberately longer than a single
queue budget.

Functional impact is limited (grace 120 still covers one full queue budget,
so retention priority still works), but the default is silently not what the
config promises.

## Root cause

The clamp bound was chosen as "cannot keep priority longer than a full queue
budget", but the intent of the knob is the opposite: it must be **at least**
one full budget (so a returning session always re-queues as retained) and may
legitimately be larger. Clamping to the wait cap makes the configured default
unrepresentable.

## Fix

Clamp to `[0, session_guardrail_max_runtime_seconds]` (already resolved in the
same function, default 1800) — the same ceiling the wait cap uses — so 300 is
valid, `0` still disables retention, and a pathological value is still
bounded. The warning then only fires for genuinely out-of-range values.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1: With `contention_queue_lease_grace_seconds: 300` and
      `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds: 120`, `_get_contention_queue_config`
      returns `lease_grace_seconds == 300.0` and logs **no** warning.
- [ ] AC2: Values above `session_guardrail_max_runtime_seconds` are clamped to
      it with a single warning; `0` disables retention (rollback path) with no
      warning; negative values clamp to 0.
- [ ] AC3: No WARNING is emitted per request for a valid configuration —
      asserted by calling the resolver repeatedly and counting warnings (the
      regression this item exists for).
- [ ] AC4: `config.yaml` comment and
      `docs/dev/contention-queue-lease-retention.md` state the corrected
      bounds and agree with the code.
- [ ] AC5: Existing contention-queue, retention and config tests stay green;
      changed-scope tests pass.

# Prefill-ETA admission guard ignores occupancy: admits queue waits that are guaranteed to time out

## Problem statement

The prefill-ETA admission guard (`proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py`, LP-0MVGDUV5E005UWBQ) was added to stop exactly the failure mode observed today: a request parks in the contention queue for up to `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` (120 s), produces nothing, and then falls back to a remote provider anyway. It compares the caller's **own** projected prefill (`eta_prefill_seconds`) against the wait budget — but not the time until a slot actually becomes available. With prefills serialised (`local_max_concurrent_prefills: 1`), another prefill is already in flight, so the true newcomer wait is its own prefill **plus** the in-flight prefill.

The proxy already computes that larger quantity and publishes it: `/llama/local/status` serves `queue_eta_seconds = prefill_eta_seconds x (busy_slots + 1)`. The guard simply does not use it. Result: the guard's own published estimate can exceed the budget while the guard still admits.

## Measured evidence (2026-10-21, window 14:56–16:49, post-restart)

Source: `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log`, `~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md`.

- 302 `contention_queue_wait` events → 40 `contention_queue_dispatch` (13 %) vs **261 `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue` (86 %)**.
- **215 of the 261 (82 %) burned the full 120 s budget** before falling back remote; aggregate wasted wait **25,804 s (7.2 h)** inside a 1.9 h wall-clock window.
- **247 of 325 full-budget losses entered the queue with `saturation=prefill`** (only 35 with `saturation=generating`) — the prefill gate, not the decode pool, is the dominant blocker.
- Admitting guard ETA distribution (n=307): median **49 s**, p75 58 s, max 100 s — i.e. consistently "within budget" against 120 s, while the real wait includes the in-flight prefill ahead of it.
- Smoking gun (15:10:45 → 15:10:57): `/llama/local/status` published `prefill_eta_seconds=43.0 queue_eta_seconds=129.0` (129 s > 120 s budget); 12 s later the guard logged `local_admission_guard decision=admit reason=within_budget eta_prefill_s=32.2 budget_s=120.0` and queued the request, which then waited the full budget and fell back remote.
- Compounding blindness: **188** `prefill_progress_unobservable` / `prefill_wait_exceeds_threshold` warnings in the same window — `lease_extended_during_prefill ... progress=None alive=False in_flight=True` repeatedly extends a lease with no visibility of prefill progress or liveness.

## Users

- As an operator, I want a request that cannot be served locally within the queue budget to fall back **immediately**, so the caller is not stalled 120 s for a guaranteed-loss wait and remote latency is paid late instead of on time.
- As a client dispatcher (herdr downtime worker, `WL-0MVHSZRZQ00482QX`), I want the proxy's admission decision to be consistent with the ETA fields it publishes, so client-side pacing is a defence in depth rather than the only defence.

## Desired change

1. **Use the occupancy-aware estimate at admission.** The guard decision must compare the *projected wait* (`queue_eta`-style: own prefill plus the remaining service of the occupied/capped prefill gate) against `wait_budget_seconds`, not the own-prefill term alone. Reuse the single shared estimator in `prefill_eta.py`; do not add a second ETA implementation.
2. **Prefer measured remaining service time where available.** The occupancy term should use the observed in-flight prefill's elapsed time and calibrated per-token prefill cost (falling back to `eta x (busy + 1)` when progress is unobservable).
3. **Fix the unobservable-progress path.** `prefill_progress_unobservable` (188 in-window) must not leave the lease extended blindly: when neither per-slot progress nor the `is_processing` liveness signal is available, the guard must treat the in-flight prefill as occupying the gate for at least the calibrated estimate, so waiters are not admitted against a phantom "free soon".
4. **Keep the fail-open contract.** Uncalibrated bucket, missing budget, or `local_admission_guard_policy: observe|off` must behave exactly as today (admit; never reject on a guess).

## Acceptance criteria

1. **AC1 — occupancy-aware refusal:** when the projected wait (`queue_eta_seconds`-equivalent, including in-flight prefill) exceeds `wait_budget_seconds` while the own-prefill ETA is within budget, the guard returns `admit=False` with `reason=eta_exceeds_budget` (or a new explicit reason) and the request falls through to the next provider without queueing. Covered by a unit test using a calibrated fixture where own ETA < budget < projected wait.
2. **AC2 — self-consistency:** a test asserts the guard's projected wait agrees with the value published as `queue_eta_seconds` by `status_estimate` for the same `(model, tokens, busy_slots)` inputs, so the two can never drift apart again.
3. **AC3 — fail-open preserved:** uncalibrated bucket, absent budget, `high` priority, and `policy=observe` all still admit (regression tests); `policy=off` does not evaluate the guard.
4. **AC4 — lease/progress:** a calibrated scenario with `prefill_progress_unobservable` (no per-slot progress, `alive=False`, `in_flight=True`) treats the in-flight prefill as occupying the gate for at least the calibrated estimate, and the decision is logged with the occupancy evidence (tests).
5. **AC5 — measured effect:** replay against the 2026-10-21 14:56–16:49 window (261 queued fallbacks, 215 at full budget, 247 prefill-saturated) reports in the work item how many of the 261 would now be refused immediately (saving their queue wait) and how many would still be admitted and dispatched, with the aggregate saved wait in seconds. The replay must show zero **lost** dispatches (i.e. no request that would have succeeded after queueing is refused) or justify each exception.
6. **AC6 — logging/observability:** the admission log line carries own ETA, occupancy term, projected wait, budget, in-flight prefill count and the resulting decision, so the failure mode is diagnosable from the log alone.
7. **AC7 — docs:** `proxy/docs/routing.md` (or the admission-guard section it references) and the `proxy/config.yaml` comment block for `local_admission_guard_policy` describe the occupancy-aware model and the `queue_eta` self-consistency requirement.
8. **AC8 — suite:** full project test suite passes via the test skill.

## Constraints

- Fail-open only: the change may refuse *additional* doomed admissions, never admit more than today.
- One estimator: no duplicate ETA maths; `prefill_eta.py` remains the single source of truth.
- No new configuration knob unless strictly required; if one is needed, name it, clamp it, and document it.
- Behaviour must remain correct for `local_max_concurrent_prefills: 0` (gate disabled → occupancy term collapses to the slot pool).
- Out of scope: reducing `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds`, changing `session_slot_pool_size`, and the ctx-size/slot trade-off (LP-0MSAOQTJS000FFVM AC6).

## Key files

- `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py` — `evaluate_admission`, `estimate_prefill_seconds`, `status_estimate`, `per_slot_prefill_eta_seconds`.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot`, `_prefill_admission_guard` call site, `_local_slot_saturation`.
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — `_get_prefill_lease_config`, lease extension on prefill progress.
- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` — `get_llama_local_status` (`queue_eta_seconds`, `prefill_budget_seconds`).
- `proxy/tests/` — admission-guard and contention-queue tests.

## Related work

- **WL-0MVHSZRZQ00482QX** (ContextHub) — herdr downtime dispatcher paces to `local_prefills_in_flight` / `prefill_gate_waiters` and defers when `queue_eta_seconds > prefill_budget_seconds`. This item is the *server-side* counterpart; the two are complementary, not alternatives (84 % of the 2026-10-21 queued-fallback events came from non-downtime agent/LAN traffic that no client-side pacing covers).
- LP-0MVGDUV5E005UWBQ — prefill-ETA admission guard (this item corrects its model).
- LP-0MVGDUUV3001XFRJ — prefill serialisation (`local_max_concurrent_prefills: 1`); publishes the gate fields.
- LP-0MVGDUVGE0024YAI — truthful capacity payload (`prefill_eta_seconds`, `queue_eta_seconds`, `prefill_budget_seconds`).
- LP-0MU498TWH008DBCI — contention-queue wake predicate must account for prefill in flight.
- LP-0MSORQVK50012Q4D — bounded cross-session contention queue.
- LP-0MVI2VRT2000V1AP — lease-owner retention priority.
- LP-0MSAOQTJS000FFVM (AC6) — local ctx-size / slot-count evaluation (1 slot x 262144 co-change).

## Risks

- **Over-refusal:** a pessimistic occupancy term could refuse waits that would have won. Mitigation: AC5 replay must show zero lost dispatches (or justify exceptions), and the change is fail-open by construction.
- **Stale in-flight estimate:** the calibrated per-token prefill cost varies with cache state; the occupancy term must use observed elapsed time for the in-flight prefill where possible.
- **Duplicate-logic drift:** mitigated by AC2's single-estimator consistency test.

## Assumptions

- `queue_eta_seconds = eta x (busy + 1)` is an acceptable upper-bound proxy for the remaining-gate-wait term when per-slot progress is unobservable (as measured, it already flagged the 129 s > 120 s case correctly).
- `saturation=prefill` in the queue-wait log line identifies gate waits reliably enough to segment the replay (247/325 of the losses).

## Evidence appendix

Reproduce the window with:

```
python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py \
    --log-dir /var/log/llama-proxy --start "2026-10-21 14:56:00"
```

then `grep -E 'contention_queue_(wait|dispatch|fallback_after_queue)|local_admission_guard'` on the same window.

# Proxy: atomic local-admission reservations + explicit fallback intent (X-Local-Preference / X-Local-Route)

## Problem statement

Today a client that wants to keep its work local has no way to *claim* local capacity before sending: it can poll `/llama/local/status` (racy — two clients can both see the same idle window; observed queue depth reached 7 while `available_slots` still reported 2 with the prefill gate saturated) and it can only learn it lost **after** the proxy has silently fallen back to a remote provider (`X-Provider: opencode` is set only post-hoc). The measured consequence (2026-10-21 14:56→17:00, 372 queue events): 261 requests queued and then went remote anyway, 215 of them after the full 120 s budget (25,804 s aggregate wasted wait).

The correct behaviour, per operator direction: **the client must not send work it cannot start.** That decision has to be made atomically — a serialised prefill gate is a single ticket that poll-and-send cannot allocate among N clients — and it has to be made *before* the work is sent. This item adds the server-side handshake; the client side is herdr `WL-0MVHSZRZQ00482QX` (ContextHub) plus its reservation follow-up.

Prerequisite: `LP-0MVICD2YW004DJPV` (occupancy-aware admission guard) — the reservation must share the guard's model or it inherits the same blind spot.

## Goal / users

- As a client dispatcher (herdr downtime worker, other agents, LAN clients), I want to reserve local capacity for a specific request before sending it, so I never queue behind a doomed wait and never silently go remote.
- As an operator, I want the proxy to answer "is my work going to run local, and if not why not" **before** the request runs, and to let me express per-request intent (`local-only` / `prefer-local` / `remote-ok`) instead of guessing.

## Desired change

1. **`POST /llama/local/reserve`** — atomic admission reservation (a gate ticket), sharing the single estimator/occupancy model from `prefill_eta.py`:
   - Request: `{estimated_tokens, session_id?, priority?, cache_state?, ttl_seconds?}`.
   - `200 {"admit": true, "reservation_id", "projected_wait_s", "ttl_s"}` — the ticket is claimed: a follow-up request carrying `X-Local-Reservation: <id>` dispatches without re-checking or queueing, subject to TTL.
   - `429 {"admit": false, "reason", "queue_eta_s", "budget_s", "retry_after_s", "X-Local-Admission*"}` — refused immediately with the reason and a retry hint; the client defers.
   - Tickets are TTL-bound (default ~5–10 s), single-use, cancellable via `DELETE /llama/local/reserve/<id>`; unclaimed tickets expire and the gate is released. A stale/missing reservation on the follow-up request falls back to today's ordinary path (never a hard failure).
   - `local-only` semantics (see 2) also available as `dry_run=true` — verdict without claiming the ticket.
2. **`X-Local-Preference: local-only | prefer-local | remote-ok`** request header, documented and additive:
   - `local-only` — never fall back remote; if the request cannot be admitted within the wait budget the proxy returns the 429 admission response **even when remote providers exist** (today it only emits that 429 when the whole chain is exhausted).
   - `prefer-local` — default, today's behaviour (queue briefly, else remote).
   - `remote-ok` — skip the local route entirely (for background/low-priority work).
3. **Response transparency headers on every response:** `X-Local-Route: local|remote|refused` and, on remote or refused, `X-Local-Fallback-Reason: <reason>` so a client can observe its loss at the moment it happens, not after.
4. **Admission guard call-site integration:** `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot` and the lease-owner retention path use the same verdict as `/reserve` (single source of truth).

## Acceptance criteria

1. **AC1 — reserve end-to-end:** a calibrated-fixture test asserts reserve returns a ticket when the occupancy-aware projected wait fits the budget, and that a follow-up request with the ticket dispatches local without queueing (assert no `contention_queue_wait` log for that request).
2. **AC2 — reserve refusal:** a calibrated-fixture test asserts reserve returns 429 with `reason`, `queue_eta_s`, `budget_s`, `retry_after_s` when the projected wait exceeds the budget, and that the refused request never enters the contention queue.
3. **AC3 — TTL and cancellation:** an expired or cancelled ticket is not honoured (falls back to ordinary path); a cancelled reservation releases the gate for the next ticket (tests).
4. **AC4 — local-only:** with `X-Local-Preference: local-only`, a request that would fall back remote instead receives the 429 admission response (with retry-after), and this behaviour is exercised when remote providers ARE available (tests).
5. **AC5 — remote-ok:** `remote-ok` never attempts the local route (assert no local attempt in the providers chain) — regression test.
6. **AC6 — route headers:** successful local responses carry `X-Local-Route: local`; remote-served responses carry `X-Local-Route: remote` and `X-Local-Fallback-Reason` matching the recorded fallback reason; refused requests carry `X-Local-Route: refused` (tests).
7. **AC7 — single estimator:** the reserve verdict and the admission-guard verdict are computed by the same function; a test asserts identical outcomes for identical inputs (mirrors `LP-0MVICD2YW004DJPV` AC2).
8. **AC8 — fail-open/backcompat:** unknown `X-Local-Preference` values, missing fields, and proxies/clients without the endpoint behave exactly as today; the endpoint and headers are additive. Uncalibrated estimator → reserve admits (never rejects on a guess).
9. **AC9 — measured effect:** replay against the 2026-10-21 14:56–16:49 window reports how many of the 261 queued fallbacks would now be refused at reserve (saving their queue wait), how many follow-up dispatches would still succeed, and the aggregate wait saved; zero lost dispatches (or each exception justified).
10. **AC10 — docs & suite:** `proxy/docs/routing.md` and the `proxy/config.yaml` comment block document the handshake, the header contract, and the interaction with `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds`/`_max_depth`; full project suite passes via the test skill.

## Constraints

- The reservation shares the occupancy-aware guard; it must not duplicate ETA maths (`prefill_eta.py` is the single source of truth).
- Fail-open: any uncertainty (uncalibrated, missing budget, `policy=observe|off`) admits like today; refusal requires a calibrated verdict AND explicit caller intent (`local-only`) or a genuinely exceeded budget.
- No new polling loops; no changes to `session_slot_pool_size` or ctx-size (that is `LP-0MSAOQTJS000FFVM` AC6).
- Security/concurrency: ticket IDs are unpredictable; reservations are per-gate (the prefill gate), scoped per provider endpoint; a ticket may not bypass the context clamp or context-bypass rules.
- Out of scope: client-side adoption (herdr `WL-0MVHSZRZQ00482QX` + ContextHub reservation follow-up), and the contention-queue sweep (`LP-0MVIKPRMD000Y97R`).

## Key files

- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` — new `/llama/local/reserve` route(s), `X-Local-Preference` parsing, route headers.
- `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py` — shared occupancy verdict (with `LP-0MVICD2YW004DJPV`).
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — guard call site, `local-only` skip-remote path, response headers.
- `proxy/proxy/priority.py` — preference/priority interaction (`local-only` vs `high` never-queues).
- `proxy/tests/` — reserve, headers, fail-open tests.

## Related work

- `LP-0MVICD2YW004DJPV` — **blocks this item**: occupancy-aware admission guard (prerequisite; share its verdict).
- `LP-0MVIKPRMD000Y97R` — blocked-by this item: contention-queue sweep once reservations land.
- `WL-0MVHSZRZQ00482QX` (ContextHub) — client-side pacing counterpart; comment LP-C0MV… (on that item) asserts the one-item-per-idle-window requirement.
- `LP-0MVGDUV5E005UWBQ`, `LP-0MVGDUUV3001XFRJ`, `LP-0MVGDUVGE0024YAI` — prefill ETA guard, serialisation gate fields, truthful capacity payload.
- `LP-0MSORQVK50012Q4D`, `LP-0MVI2VRT2000V1AP`, `LP-0MU498TWH008DBCI` — contention queue, lease retention, prefill-aware wake.

## Risks

- **Ticket misuse / hoarding:** a client reserving and not sending would starve others. Mitigation: short TTL, single-use, cancellation endpoint, monitoring of `reserved-but-unused` (additive status field).
- **Over-refusal on `local-only`:** a wrong verdict means remote latency, not a failure — and fail-open design means refusal needs calibration.
- **Drift between `status`, guard, and reserve:** mitigated by the single-estimator AC7.

# Contention-queue sweep: collapse depth/wait once reservations land

## Problem statement

The contention queue exists to convert wait time into probability of staying local. Measured on 2026-10-21 (window 14:56→17:00, 372 queue events): 43 wins (median wait 65 s) versus 329 losses, of which 283 (86 %) would have needed ≥120 s under any cap — i.e. hopeless. A fixed budget and depth are load-shedding knobs that cannot separate the two cases (see `LP-0MVICD2YW004DJPV` scope note; queue depth reached 7 in-window while 261 requests still burned the budget). Once reservations exist (`LP-0MVIKPCSG002B0NL`), cooperating clients no longer rely on the queue: they claim a ticket or defer. The queue then serves only stragglers and can be collapsed without sacrificing wins.

## Goal / users

- As an operator, I want the fallback queue to be a small safety net for non-cooperating clients, not the primary waiting mechanism for cooperative ones.
- As a client, I want my only waits to be ticket-backed (reserved) waits or explicit in-client deferrals, never an invisible proxy-side 120 s park.

## Desired change

1. After `LP-0MVIKPCSG002B0NL` ships and has been live for an observation window, lower `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` from 120 s to a sweep value (~15–30 s) and `contention_queue_max_depth` from 8 to ~1–2, per the measured replacement data.
2. Track the retained-win rate during the sweep: ticket-backed dispatches keep the oracle winnable-wait share; the residual queue wins lost to the shorter budget must be accounted against reservation-driven wins (replay from `LP-0MVIKPCSG002B0NL` AC9 plus new telemetry).
3. Keep the numbers as config (already are) so the sweep is a two-line change with a documented rollback.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **AC1 — sweep plan:** a written plan in this item with the target values, the trigger (reservations live + N days of telemetry), and the rollback path; values justified by the win/loss wait distributions in the evidence appendix.
2. **AC2 — guard consistency:** the shorter budget flows into the admission guard's `wait_budget_seconds` and the reservation endpoint's budget automatically (same resolver — no second constant), with tests.
3. **AC3 — residual-queue telemetry:** counts of (a) ticket-backed dispatches, (b) residual queue wins ≤ sweep budget, (c) residual queue losses and their aggregate wait, reported for the observation window; the sweep is only flipped when (a) >> (b) is observed (or is declared acceptable).
4. **AC4 — docs:** `proxy/config.yaml` comments and `proxy/docs/routing.md` describe the queue as a straggler safety net with reservations as the primary path.

## Constraints

- The sweep must not run before reservations ship (`LP-0MVIKPCSG002B0NL`); dep edge enforced.
- Fail-open semantics of the guard unchanged (uncalibrated → admit).
- Out of scope: queue removal (a zero-wait proxy has no local concurrency tolerance at all), slot count, ctx-size.

## Key files

- `proxy/config.yaml` — `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds`, `contention_queue_max_depth`.
- `proxy/proxy/router.py` (`_get_contention_queue_config`), `proxy/proxy/priority.py` (budget resolver).
- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` (status: `contention_queue_depth`, new reservation telemetry).
- `proxy/tests/` — budget-resolver tests.

# Epic: minimise local LLM tail latency (prefill-bound first-byte tails)

## Goal (user story)

As an operator/agent driving the proxy, I want a local Qwen3 request to either
answer inside a bounded budget or be routed remote quickly, so that the
multi-minute stalls that dominate the local tail disappear and the worst-case
latency across the whole provider set is bounded by tens of seconds rather than
minutes.

## Measured baseline (24 h window, 2026-10-20 23:31 → 2026-10-21 23:31 IST)

All figures from `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log*` and `llama-server.log`.

| Signal | Baseline |
|---|---|
| Local dispatch → first byte (`dispatch_first_byte_ms`, n=606) | p50 **8.9 s**, p90 **96.5 s**, p99 **443 s**, max **592 s** |
| Local dispatches with first byte > 60 s / > 120 s | **91** / **48** of 606 |
| Same, `cache_state=warm` subset (n=419) | p90 **88.7 s**, max 592 s |
| llama-server prompt-eval duration | p50 16 s, p90 **189 s**, max **591 s** |
| Prompt-eval throughput | p10 **77 t/s**, p50 211 t/s (20 k+ batches), p90 302 t/s |
| `local_admission_guard` | 1 965 admit (`within_budget`) / **415 reject** (`eta_exceeds_budget`) |
| `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue` | **1 481** (`reason=local_lease_active`) + 252 unlabelled, all after the full 120 s wait |
| `orphan_cleanup` vs `lease_verified_active` | **298** vs **6** |
| Local streams > 60 s that were orphan-cleaned mid-span yet finished later | **81** of 118 |
| `contention_queue_wait ... saturation=` samples | **1 827** prefill vs 468 generating |
| `prefill_progress_unobservable` | 1 242 |

Interpretation: `dispatch_to_first_byte` ≈ total local response time, so the tail
is **prefill**, not decode. A 40–80 k-token prefill costs 130–500 s at the
measured throughput, `local_max_concurrent_prefills: 1` makes one such prefill
block everything behind it, and the lease bookkeeping frees slots that are still
working (298 cleanups vs 6 verified alive).

## Scope

**In scope** — five children:

1. `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` 120 → 60.
2. Prefill-ETA guard on the **direct (free-slot) dispatch** path.
3. Orphan-cleanup / `/slots` liveness fix (fail-closed, cancel upstream).
4. llama-server `ubatch-size` 1024 → 2048 (benchmark-gated).
5. ETA-aware admission ordering + prefill heartbeat + prefill deadline.

**Explicitly out of scope** (do not fold into a child):

- **Warm-cache threshold is unchanged** — `local_large_context_warm_cache_threshold`
  stays 120000 and `local_large_context_economic_ceiling_ratio` stays 0.4578.
- **No TTS isolation** — TTS stays on the shared GPU; child 4 is the ubatch
  change only.
- No prompt-compaction change (`compaction_trigger_ratio` stays 0) and no
  slot-pool change (`session_slot_pool_size` stays 2).

## Acceptance criteria

1. Local `dispatch_first_byte_ms` over a ≥24 h deployed window: p90 ≤ 45 s
   (baseline 96.5 s), p99 ≤ 120 s (baseline 443 s), max ≤ 180 s (baseline 592 s).
2. Zero local dispatches whose first byte exceeds the configured local wait
   budget (baseline 48 > 120 s): every over-budget projection is refused
   up-front and routed remote.
3. Orphan churn collapses: `orphan_cleanup` ≤ 5 % of local dispatches (baseline
   298 cleanups ≈ 49 % of 606) and **zero** streams that are orphan-cleaned and
   then go on to finish (baseline 81).
4. No regression: remote provider p50/p90 unchanged, local decode throughput and
   aggregate prefill tokens/s not reduced, full test suite green.
5. Each child lands with its own tests, config/docs updates, and a measured
   before/after recorded on the item (reuse the LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD measurement
   approach).
6. `local_large_context_warm_cache_threshold` and
   `local_large_context_economic_ceiling_ratio` are unchanged at completion.

## Risks / notes

- **Measurement contamination:** child 4 needs a llama-server restart, which
  empties the prompt cache and biases first-byte stats cold. Sequence child 4's
  measurement window so it is not mixed with the others, and record the
  restart in the child's comment.
- **Single budget source:** children 1, 2 and 5 all reason about the same wait
  budget (`contention_queue_max_wait_seconds`). Do not introduce a second,
  competing budget; the ETA estimator and the guard must stay one implementation.
- **Load shifting:** refusing more local work pushes traffic onto rate-limited
  remote tiers (munitoai-free 3 rpm, opencode). Watch 429s and fallback counts in
  the same window; a latency win that produces remote 429 storms is not a win.
- **Budget values:** 60 s for the contention queue was chosen from a separate
  investigation (see child 1); 30 s was the fallback if the evidence disagreed.
  This analysis found no evidence contradicting 60 s.

## Related work

- LP-0MVGDUV5E005UWBQ — prefill-ETA admission guard (queue-entry only today).
- LP-0MVGDUUV3001XFRJ — prefill serialisation (`local_max_concurrent_prefills: 1`).
- LP-0MUXTW4MD003TVIC — `/slots` unobservable during long prefills.
- LP-0MUXQ5QL40027VZ4 — progress unobservable under load.
- LP-0MUGQHPJ50046LV8 — watchdog released the lease but never cancelled upstream.
- LP-0MSUO6XRP001MCB2 — active-stream verification in orphan cleanup.
- LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD — 24 h measurement of local admission impact (reuse its
  methodology for the before/after on each child).

# Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want a request that cannot get a local slot to spend at most
**60 s** in the contention queue before it falls through to a remote provider,
so the dead waiting time on the local path halves without losing the
lease-owner retention benefit.

Part of epic **LP-0MVIPY7QX0027XVD** (minimise local LLM tail latency).

## Evidence (24 h window, 2026-10-20 23:31 → 2026-10-21 23:31 IST)

- `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue` fired **1 481** times with
  `reason=local_lease_active` (plus 252 with no reason), every one after
  `queued_duration=120.00s` — i.e. the full budget was spent and the request
  went remote anyway.
- The config comment for `contention_queue_lease_grace_seconds` already records
  the same pattern from the 2026-10-19→20 measurement: 4 947 of 5 805 queued
  waits (85 %) were abandoned, and the prefill-ETA guard exists precisely
  because "the wait is a guaranteed loss".
- Local first byte is p50 8.9 s but p90 96.5 s / p99 443 s (n=606), i.e. the
  queue is not absorbing the tail, it is relocating it.

## Proposed change

Single knob:

```yaml
server:
  contention_queue_max_wait_seconds: 60   # was 120
```

- Keep `contention_queue_max_depth: 8` and
  `contention_queue_lease_grace_seconds: 300` unchanged.
- Keep `contention_queue_policy: queue` unchanged.
- No new knobs; no code change expected beyond config/docs if the value is read
  per request (confirm on implementation; document if a proxy restart is
  required).

**Why 60 and not 30:** a separate investigation concluded 60 s is the optimum
for this queue. This analysis has no evidence that contradicts it — the queued
population is dominated by retained sessions whose prompt cache is warm (the
case the retention rule exists to protect), where a 60 s wait can still succeed
— so 60 is adopted. 30 s is the documented fallback if the measurement after
this change shows the queue is still pure loss (i.e. the abandoned share does
not fall).

## Acceptance criteria

1. `server.contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` is 60 in `proxy/config.yaml`, with
   the comment updated to record the baseline (1 481 full-120 s fallbacks) and
   the reason for the value.
2. A queued local request never waits longer than 60 s before falling back
   (test covering the timeout path).
3. Lease-owner retention behaviour is unchanged: the existing retention tests
   (`contention_queue_retention` / `lease_grace`) pass unmodified.
4. Docs updated (`proxy/docs/routing.md` or wherever the contention queue is
   described) and the restart/reload requirement documented.
5. A ≥24 h deployed measurement shows `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue`
   `queued_duration` bounded by 60 s and no increase in fallbacks *per request*;
   record numbers on this item.
6. Full test suite green; commit + hash recorded.

## Risks

- Shortening the wait moves some retained sessions to remote earlier; if the
  remote tier is rate-limited (munitoai-free 3 rpm) this can produce 429s.
  Watch 429s and `Fallback triggered ... rate_limited` in the same window.
- If the ETA guard (LP-0MVGDUV5E005UWBQ) rejects prefill projections above the
  budget, a shorter queue only changes how long the request takes to discover
  it cannot be served — that is the intended behaviour.

## Related work

- LP-0MVGDUV5E005UWBQ — prefill-ETA admission guard (budget consumer).
- LP-0MVGDUUV3001XFRJ — prefill serialisation (why slots are busy for minutes).
- Epic LP-0MVIPY7QX0027XVD — parent.

# Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want **any** local dispatch whose projected prefill cannot
finish inside the local wait budget to be refused up-front — even when a slot is
free — so we never start a three-to-ten-minute prefill that the caller will
abandon.

Part of epic **LP-0MVIPY7QX0027XVD** (minimise local LLM tail latency).

## Evidence (24 h window, 2026-10-20 23:31 → 2026-10-21 23:31 IST)

- `local_admission_guard` evaluated **2 380** times: 1 965 `decision=admit
  reason=within_budget`, 415 `decision=reject reason=eta_exceeds_budget`. The
  rejected ETAs had median **176 s** and max **876 s** against
  `budget_s=120.0`.
- The guard, per its own config comment, runs **before entering the contention
  queue** only ("Before entering the contention queue the proxy costs the
  projected local prefill … and compares it with the caller's wait budget").
  A request that finds a free slot is dispatched with no ETA ceiling.
- Result: **48 of 606** local dispatches had a first byte after >120 s, and 91
  after >60 s (p50 8.9 s, p90 96.5 s, p99 443 s, max 592 s).
- llama-server prompt-eval durations confirm the cost: p50 16 s, p90 189 s, max
  591 s, at 77–302 t/s depending on size and contention.

So the guard already exists and is calibrated; it is simply bypassed on the
direct-dispatch path.

## Proposed change

1. Reuse the existing prefill-ETA estimator (observed `dispatch_first_byte_ms`,
   keyed by model + context bucket, rolling window — as used by
   LP-0MVGDUV5E005UWBQ) on the **direct dispatch** path, before the local
   request is sent upstream.
2. If projected prefill > the local wait budget, skip local and fall through to
   the next provider in the existing chain with an explicit log reason, e.g.
   `local_admission_guard decision=reject reason=eta_exceeds_budget_direct`.
3. Keep exactly one budget source (`contention_queue_max_wait_seconds`, lowered
   to 60 s by the sibling child); do not add a second knob.
4. Keep the queue-entry guard unchanged — this is the same decision applied one
   step earlier.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A request whose projected prefill exceeds the budget is **never** dispatched
   locally, including when a local slot is free (unit test with a stubbed
   estimator).
2. A request whose projected prefill fits the budget is still dispatched locally
   on a free slot (no regression for the common case).
3. Behaviour is identical to today when the estimator has no samples yet
   (cold start): document the conservative default and cover it with a test.
4. Refusals are observable: log line with the projected ETA, the budget, and the
   chosen fallback provider; counter available on
   `/llama/local/status` if cheap to add.
5. Docs updated (routing/prefill section) and the config comment that claims the
   guard is queue-entry-only is corrected.
6. ≥24 h deployed measurement: local `dispatch_first_byte_ms` > budget ≈ 0
   (baseline 48), p99 ≤ 120 s; record numbers on the item.
7. Full test suite green; commit + hash recorded.

## Risks

- **Estimator quality:** the ETA model is empirical; a mis-estimate either
  refuses work the box could have finished (lost local capacity) or admits a
  slow prefill (tail returns). Log projected vs observed so the estimator can be
  recalibrated, and keep the safety net of the prefill deadline child.
- **Cold start / new session shapes:** a session with a large but unusual prompt
  may project badly; the estimator's per-context-bucket history is the guard.
- **Load shifting:** refusals push work to rate-limited remotes — watch 429s.

## Related work

- LP-0MVGDUV5E005UWBQ — prefill-ETA admission guard (queue-entry implementation
  this extends).
- LP-0MVGDUUV3001XFRJ — prefill serialisation.
- LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD — 24 h measurement methodology.
- Epic LP-0MVIPY7QX0027XVD — parent.
